title: Golden Triangle Classic
desc: The essential first-China trip: the Great Wall, Forbidden City and Temple of Heaven, then the Terracotta Army and Xi'an's city wall, finishing on the Bund skyline.
itin: Arrive Beijing; Tian'anmen Square & evening Peking duck
Temple of Heaven, then high-speed rail to Xi'an (4.5h)
City Wall bike ride & Muslim Quarter food tour; rail to Shanghai
Bund skyline, Yu Garden & French Concession
Optional: Suzhou gardens day trip (see Route 5)

seasonal.d: Run it in Oct for Mutianyu's autumn maples or Sep for crisp wall-top rides; avoid Golden Week (Oct 1–7) when queues triple.
seasonal.adj: Start mornings before 9:00; book Forbidden City tickets 7 days ahead.

budget.d: Metro + 2nd-class HSR instead of private transfers; chain hotels (Ji Hotel/Hanting) at ¥250–350; eat at canteens and small restaurants.
budget.adj: Book all attraction tickets on official mini-programs for the list price; skip optional cable car at Mutianyu.

family.d: One extra night per city; add Disneyland or Shanghai Science Museum; cable car both ways at the Wall plus the toboggan.
family.adj: Ask for mild, non-spicy dishes; keep evenings free for hotel pools.

title: Sichuan Natural Wonders
desc: Pandas, the world's biggest Buddha, and a turquoise fairyland — one province, three icons. Best in autumn when Jiuzhaigou blazes with color.
itin: Panda Base morning; Sichuan opera night
HSR to Leshan; Giant Buddha & river boat
Return Chengdu; fly to Jiuzhai Huanglong
Jiuzhaigou full days (Y-shaped valley, Five Flower Lake)
Huanglong calcified pools or fly back

seasonal.d: Jiuzhaigou at peak color (after Oct 15) with Golden Week crowds gone; Huanglong's calcified pools at their most vivid.
seasonal.adj: Fly Chengdu→Jiuzhai Huanglong early; enter the park by 8:00 to beat tour groups.

budget.d: Run Nov–Mar off-season: Jiuzhaigou tickets drop ~50% and hotels to ¥150–250; winter flights are cheap.
budget.adj: Wear spikes (rentable) for icy boardwalks in Dec–Feb; park shuttle buses cover all viewpoints.

family.d: Panda Base first thing (cubs are active at feeding time); Leshan by river cruise so kids skip 500 steps; Jiuzhaigou in easy shuttle stages.
family.adj: Pack snacks and altitude-awareness (park is 2,000–3,000 m).

title: Avatar Peaks & Li River
desc: China's two most surreal landscapes: the pillar forests of Avatar and the karst river of every Chinese painting.
itin: Glass bridge; evening rail to Guilin

seasonal.d: After-rain fog makes the pillar forests otherworldly; higher river levels keep the Li River rafts steady and safe.
seasonal.adj: Check the Zhangjiajie weather app — go up on the first clear morning.

budget.d: Stay in Wulingyuan town or Yangshuo county guesthouses (¥150–220); book the park + shuttle pass on the official site.
budget.adj: Skip the glass bridge if you want the cheapest combo; walk Yulong River's riverside path instead of rafting.

family.d: Glass bridge thrills are gentle enough for most kids; take the big Li River boat (stable) and reserve life jackets on rafts; e-bike with a child seat for Yangshuo countryside.
family.adj: Pace to one big sight per day — the park itself is exhausting.

title: Silk Road & Tibet
desc: From the Terracotta Army to Mogao's thousand Buddhas to the Potala Palace — the epic trans-continental China. Requires Tibet travel permits (booked via agency).
itin: Night train or flight to Dunhuang
Mogao Caves + Singing Sand Dunes sunset
Barkhor old town & Sera Monastery debates
Optional: Namtso lake, then depart Lhasa

seasonal.d: Dunhuang is bearable and Lhasa skies are blue; avoid Jul–Aug when rain and road closures disrupt the desert-to-plateau leg.
seasonal.adj: Book Mogao Caves tickets weeks ahead — daily numbers are capped.

budget.d: Take the Qinghai–Tibet Railway sleeper into Lhasa instead of flying — saves ~¥800 and helps acclimatization; hostel in Dunhuang.
budget.adj: Bring a CPAP-friendly plan for sleep at 3,650 m; permits included via your agency.

family.d: Three acclimatization days in Lhasa before big sights; skip Everest base camp and Namtso overnight; Mogao kids' audio guide.
family.adj: Altitude medicine from a doctor before departure; keep first two Lhasa days light.

title: Jiangnan Water Towns
desc: Classical gardens, lantern-lit canals and the poetry of West Lake — the refined east-China classic, all linked by 30-minute high-speed trains.
itin: Shanghai Tower & French Concession; rail to Suzhou
Rail to Tongxiang; Wuzhen Xizha (stay overnight)
Morning canals; rail to Hangzhou; West Lake

seasonal.d: Apricot blossom and rain make gardens and canals dreamlike; Oct–Nov osmanthus season works just as well.
seasonal.adj: Pack an umbrella — the rain is part of the charm; weekday visits avoid tour crowds.

budget.d: Intercity HSR + stay outside Wuzhen's west gate; off-peak garden tickets; meals at locals' eateries off the canal.
budget.adj: Buy combined garden passes in Suzhou; the Humble Administrator's Garden alone is ¥70–90.

family.d: West Lake boat ride + silk museum DIY; half-day in Wuzhen's east gate; Lion Grove's rock maze delights kids.
family.adj: Choose Lion Grove over the (quieter, less playful) Humble Administrator's Garden if time is short.

title: Yunnan & Tropical Escape
desc: Old-town romance under snow mountains, then three days of turquoise beaches — the ultimate contrast trip.
itin: Arrive Lijiang; old town canals & night market
Jade Dragon Snow Mountain day trip
Black Dragon Pool & Baisha village; fly to Sanya

seasonal.d: Lijiang under clear skies, Sanya at 25°C with empty beaches; avoids the Jul–Aug rain and heat.
seasonal.adj: Book Lijiang→Sanya flights early — winter is peak for Hainan.

budget.d: Train Dali→Lijiang; off-season guesthouses at ¥150; apartment-style hotels in Sanya Bay for kitchenettes.
budget.adj: Use city buses in Lijiang; skip the ¥170 Jade Dragon Snow Mountain ropeway if the budget is tight.

family.d: E-bike ride around Erhai with a child seat; Sanya's Yalong Bay for calm swimming; half-day on Wuzhizhou Island.
family.adj: Sunblock and life jackets — Hainan sun is intense even in winter.

title: Central Plains Ancient Capitals
desc: The cradle of Chinese civilization: the Longmen Grottoes, Shaolin kung fu on Mount Song, then a living Ming–Qing walled city.
itin: Arrive Luoyang; evening at the Old Town & Liyang Gate lights
Longmen Grottoes morning; White Horse Temple afternoon
Bus to Dengfeng; Shaolin Temple, Pagoda Forest & kung fu show
Rail to Pingyao via Taiyuan; old city wall walk at sunset
Rishengchang Bank & county yamen; depart from Taiyuan

seasonal.d: Luoyang's peony festival plus Longmen Grottoes at their freshest; Pingyao in crisp Sep–Oct light.
seasonal.adj: Peony show tickets sell out — book with the festival app; arrive at Longmen before 9:00.

budget.d: HSR to Zhengzhou/Luoyang; guesthouses just outside Pingyao's wall (¥180); Shaolin + Pagoda Forest combo ticket.
budget.adj: Walk the wall in Pingyao at sunset — free and beautiful.

family.d: Shaolin kung-fu show with monk interaction; dress-up photo session at Pingyao's ticket ‘banks’; electric carts inside Longmen.
family.adj: The Longmen west bank is a long walk — use the cart for little legs.

title: Yunnan Highlands
desc: Erhai lake loops, Naxi old-town romance under snow peaks, then Tibet-flavored Shangri-La with a river-gorge trek on the way.
itin: Arrive Dali; old town lanes & Three Pagodas
E-bike loop along Erhai to Shuanglang; sunset cruise
Rail/bus to Lijiang; old town canals & Black Dragon Pool
Jade Dragon Snow Mountain day trip (or Tiger Leaping Gorge trek)
Drive to Shangri-La; Dukezong old town & Songzanlin Monastery
Depart from Shangri-La (or extend to Pudacuo Park)

seasonal.d: Shangri-La's meadows turn gold and Meili Snow Mountain shows its peak; May–Jun adds rhododendron blooms.
seasonal.adj: Lijiang→Shangri-La by bus gives the best gradual acclimatization.

budget.d: Buses instead of private cars; guesthouses in Dukezong old town; the free Tiger Leaping Gorge viewpoint section.
budget.adj: Trek only the easy first section unless you are a hiker — the full gorge is serious.

family.d: Jade Dragon Glacier Park cable car with portable oxygen; Tiger Leaping from the platform, not the trail; elevator guesthouses in Lijiang old town.
family.adj: Keep children hydrated; descend if anyone feels dizzy — symptoms fade below 2,500 m.

title: Chengdu Evening Snack Walk
desc: Self-guided evening snack walk in UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy Chengdu: sample Sichuan street snacks and light hotpot-style bites around classic old-town lanes (Kuanzhai / Jinli corridor)—not a ticketed tour. Spice levels run medium–high; many stalls are cashless (Alipay/WeChat) with limited English menus. Vendors and hours change—verify on the day. No booking or buy CTA; this is editorial pacing only.
itin: Self-guided start near Kuanzhai Alley; skim spice/cashless tips before you eat
Wander alley snack stalls: dan dan–style noodles, skewers, cold dishes—order small plates to share
Continue toward Jinli-area snack streets for sweets/tea; pace yourself on chili oil
Metro/taxi back; keep water handy. Not a sold tour—no guide booking required
best: Year-round evenings; cooler months easier for spice
